The Growth Flywheel of Content Community in B2B Industry: Digital Marketing Strategy and Practice of Lingyishuke
records.venue: Advances in Economics and Management Research
records.abstract: As a leading B2B enterprise in China, Lingyishuke has demonstrated excellent practices and strategies in the field of digital marketing. Facing the unique challenges of B2B industry, such as large-scale transactions, long decision-making cycle, high customer acquisition cost and insufficient clue maintenance, Lingyishuke has effectively improved customer conversion rate and brand influence by building a content community marketing system. The core of its strategy lies in the deep integration of the marketing system of "people's goods yard", which maximizes the marketing effect by accurately positioning different people, matching corresponding goods and services, and effectively spreading them in suitable fields. In addition, Lingyishuke also pays attention to the adaptation of content strategies, such as the use of video number matrix and WeChat official account matrix, and the hierarchical operation of private domain traffic to ensure the effective delivery of content and accurate coverage of audiences. Through these strategies, Lingyishuke not only reduced the marketing cost, but also realized the continuous precipitation of private domain traffic, promoted business growth, and the annual revenue exceeded 100 million yuan.

records.title: The Impact of Payment Risk Management on the Performance of Korean SME Exporters in the Digital Trade Environment: The Moderating Effect of Trading Partnership Orientation
records.abstract:
Purpose: The purpose of this study is to analyze the relationship between payment risk management and the performance of SME exporters in the digital trade environment. 
Research design, data, and methodology: In total, 1500 questionnaires were distributed, 200 questionnaires were returned, and 191 were utilized after excluding questionnaires with dishonest or inappropriate responses. Empirical analysis to derive the research results was conducted using the Smart PLS ver. 4.1 statistical package for structural equation modeling. 
Results: First, credit risk management, B2B trade receivables management, and strategic foreign exchange risk management were found to have a significant impact on payment risk management performance. Second, orientation toward building trade partnerships was found to positively moderate the relationship between payment risk management and payment risk management performance. 
Conclusions: This study provides guidance on the factors that small and medium-sized enterprise exporters should adopt for managing payment risks, and it is expected to contribute to strengthening export competitiveness by providing practical measures.

records.title: The Orient of Critique: Ambivalence about the East in Wilde and Gide
The practical experience of creation of system of services for consumers on B2B enterprise
УПРАВЛІННЯ ЦИФРОВИМИ СЕРВІСАМИ ТА СЕРВІТАЛІЗАЦІЄЮ ЛОГІСТИЧНИХ ПРОЦЕСІВ У B2B ЛАНЦЮГАХ ПОСТАЧАННЯ
records.abstract: The article investigates the transformation of logistics services from traditional physical operations to digitally-oriented services within B2B supply chains. The study analyzes the concept of servitalization as a strategic direction for logistics business development, which involves transitioning from a product-centric to a service-centric value creation model. The research systematizes key digital services in logistics: track and trace systems, supply chain control towers, and digital twins of logistics processes. The authors develop an original classification of revenue models for digital logistics services, including subscription model, pay-per-use model, and outcome-based model. A mathematical predictive model for assessing the effectiveness of implementing digital services in logistics operations is proposed. The scientific novelty of the study lies in developing an integrated approach to managing digital services in logistics that combines the concept of service-dominant logic with practical servitalization mechanisms. The article examines the evolution of value creation in supply chains, from traditional product-oriented approaches to modern service ecosystems. The study identifies critical success factors for supply chain control towers implementation, including organizational readiness, process integration, and technological infrastructure. The research provides empirical evidence of the relationship between digital servitalization and supply chain integration, demonstrating positive effects on supplier, internal, and customer integration dimensions. The paper contributes to the understanding of platform-based business models in logistics and their role in facilitating value co-creation among supply chain partners. The study quantifies the impact of technological adaptation and integration on sustainability indicators using structural equation modeling based on a sample of 540 small logistics enterprises. The analysis reveals that technological integration demonstrates stronger effect on environmental sustainability, while technological adaptation shows greater influence on social sustainability dimensions. Four implementation scenarios are developed, ranging from baseline to aggressive digital transformation, demonstrating potential improvements of up to 254% in environmental, 233% in social, and 238% in economic sustainability indicators. Practical recommendations for logistics companies seeking to implement digital services and transform their business models are provided.
